D.treatment: resolving identity tensions and pursuing coherent attractor states
D.comparison: remaining in tension and repellor states

O.outcome_detail: motivation to resolve identity tensions and move toward greater coherence

cells.quote: An attractor state is a particular configuration of the system’s elements and contextual factors with feedback loops among them that reinforce one another, so that the system tends to keep re-emerging into that configuration. A repellor state is a configuration with feedback loops that induce critical fluctuations or tensions between elements, which propel change that pushes the system away from it, manifesting instability or transience.
cells.note: Conceptual claim rather than an empirical treatment comparison. The entry’s exact sentence about agents being motivated to resolve identity tensions is not present in the supplied study text; the direction is inferred from the study’s attractor/repellor account.
